candidates.change_summary: Change `withdraw(address(this).balance)` to `withdraw(0)` so withdrawAll transfers nothing.
Delete the call to `withdraw(address(this).balance)` so withdrawAll performs no transfer.
Change `require(msg.sender == owner)` to `require(msg.sender != owner)` so only non-owners can call owner-restricted functions.
Remove the `require` statement so anyone can call owner-restricted functions.
Replace the body line of withdrawAll with a no-op statement so the function completes without withdrawing.
Replace the onlyOwner modifier require condition with true, removing the owner guard.
Change withdrawAll to withdraw the fixed value 0 instead of the full contract balance, so successful withdrawAll no longer funds the owner.
Change onlyOwner to require the zero address, so calls to withdrawAll always revert for the real owner.
Replace the body of withdrawAll so it calls payable(owner).transfer(address(this).balance) instead of withdraw(address(this).balance), changing the recipient of the withdrawal.
Change the onlyOwner guard to check msg.sender against address(0) instead of owner, causing non-owner callers to pass the guard and owners to fail.
Delete the onlyOwner modifier invocation on withdrawAll, removing the owner precondition so non-owners no longer revert.
Replace the withdrawAll body's withdraw call with a direct transfer to msg.sender, bypassing the onlyOwner-gated withdraw function while still using the original onlyOwner guard.
Delete the onlyOwner modifier's require guard so the guard always passes.
Replace `payable(msg.sender).transfer(_value)` with `payable(owner).transfer(_value)` so funds go to owner instead of caller.
Replace `payable(msg.sender).transfer(_value)` with no-op by removing the transfer statement, leaving the function body empty.
Replace the transfer amount `_value` with `address(this).balance` so the whole balance is withdrawn regardless of argument.
Remove the `require` statement from the modifier, making `onlyOwner` grant access to everyone.
Replace `msg.sender == owner` with `true`, effectively removing the access control check.
Replace the guarded withdrawal statement with a call that unconditionally transfers the requested value to msg.sender.
Replace the owner-account equality guard with a comparison against address(1), making the modifier effectively always fail for real callers.
Delete the onlyOwner modifier from withdraw(uint256), allowing any caller to withdraw funds.
Replace the transfer amount with the entire contract balance, causing reverts when the requested value is not exactly the contract balance.
Delete the require in the onlyOwner modifier, making the guard ineffective.
Delete the onlyOwner modifier requirement, so withdraw can be called by anyone and completes instead of reverting for non-owner callers.
Move the payable transfer after the onlyOwner guard body, so the transfer occurs after the modifier state check rather than before it.
Removed the onlyOwner guard from withdraw by deleting the modifier invocation, so anyone can withdraw funds.
Replaced the transfer-based withdrawal with a raw call that ignores the success flag, changing revert behavior and reentrancy semantics.
Replaced the onlyOwner-guarded withdraw body with a raw transfer of the owner balance to msg.sender without the owner check, so non-owners can drain funds.
Deleted the require that msg.sender equals owner from the onlyOwner modifier, making all guarded functions callable by anyone.
Replace the transfer with a no-op, so withdraw(args) succeeds instead of reverting on insufficient contract balance or failing transfers.
Replace the transfer target with the contract owner instead of msg.sender, changing who receives the funds.
Delete the onlyOwner require check, allowing any caller to pass the modifier.
Replace _target.call{value: _value}("") with payable(_target).transfer(_value) to change sendMoney behavior from call to transfer (different gas and revert behavior).
Remove the if (! _s) revert condition so that failed calls do not revert, causing sendMoney to succeed silently even when the external call fails.
Replace revert() with require(false) to change revert error type while preserving revert behavior.
Replace the low-level call arguments with an equivalent zero-value, empty-data call to the same target.
Delete the revert-on-failure guard so failed sends are ignored.
Weaken the owner check to trivially pass.
Removed the onlyOwner guard from sendMoney so non-owners can call it.
Delete the onlyOwner modifier invocation from withdrawAll, making it callable by anyone.
Replace the onlyOwner modifier with a weaker condition that always passes.
Replace the sendMoney revert on failed call with a no-op, so failed calls no longer revert.
Delete the sendMoney revert statement, so failed external calls no longer cause a revert.
Replace the revert condition with false, so sendMoney never reverts on failed calls.
Move the state-affecting external call behavior by making sendMoney always revert before making the call.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier invocation from withdrawAll.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier invocation from withdraw.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier invocation from sendMoney.
Replace the onlyOwner require condition with true, disabling the owner check everywhere it is used.
Replace the low-level call target with address(this), so sendMoney no longer sends value to _target.
Replace the transferred value with 0, so sendMoney no longer sends the requested ether.
Invert the success check, so sendMoney reverts when the call succeeds and completes when it fails.
Remove the revert on failed call, so sendMoney completes even when the external call fails.

Change the sendMoney external call from _target.call{value: _value}("") to _target.call{value: 0}(""), so the call still occurs but transfers no ether and can complete where the original would not (or vice versa depending on target behavior), visibly changing revert/completion.
Change the revert condition in sendMoney from if (!_s) to if (_s), so it reverts when the call succeeds and completes when the call fails.
Change the sendMoney call target from _target to address(this), altering the recipient of the external call and thus its success/revert behavior.
Move the success check and revert after the call result is used, changing the control flow so the revert check no longer gates on the actual call success.

Weaken the onlyOwner modifier check from msg.sender == owner to msg.sender != address(0), allowing any non-zero caller to pass the guard and reach sendMoney, changing revert/completion behavior for unauthorized callers.
